title: A Chitosan Based, Laser Activated Thin Film Surgical Adhesive, 'SurgiLux': Preparation and Demonstration
protocol: Prepare a 2% (v/v) solution of acetic acid using deionized water in a clean glass beaker.
Weigh 0.02% (w/v) of indocyanine green in a sterile Eppendorf tube wrapped in silver foil.
Transfer approximately 1 ml of the dilute acetic acid solution to the tube with dye and shake gently.
Dissolve the dye by shaking, then transfer the solubilized ICG into the beaker containing acetic acid.
Add 2% (w/v) chitosan powder to the beaker and mix using a sterile magnetic stirrer covered with Parafilm and wrapped in silver foil.
Mix the contents at about 125 rpm for 72 hours at room temperature in a laminar flow hood.
Centrifuge the mixture at 15,000 x g for 15 minutes at 4 °C to remove particulate matter.
Transfer the green SurgiLux solution into a clean glass beaker and cover it with Parafilm wrapped in silver foil.
Store the green SurgiLux solution in a refrigerator for 12 hours to increase viscosity.
Dispense 8 ml of cold SurgiLux solution into a clean Petri dish of 95 mm diameter using a sterile syringe.
Gently tilt the plate to ensure complete coverage by the solution.
Remove any visible bubbles in the solution using the tip of a sterile needle.
Cover the dish in silver foil.
Place the covered dish in a refrigerator for 20 minutes.
Carefully remove the Petri dish from the refrigerator.
Place the Petri dish in a laminar flow hood and cover with silver foil.
Leave the solution to evaporate for 3 weeks.
Score the outer edges of the clear green SurgiLux film in the Petri dish.
Gently peel the SurgiLux film away from the dish surface.
Store the circular SurgiLux films in the Petri dish wrapped in silver foil under dry conditions.
Cut a piece of bovine tissue to a size of 15 mm wide and 20 mm length.
Dissect the tissue in a straight line using a Number 10 surgical blade.
Approximate the two pieces of tissue so that their edges are touching but not overlapping.
Gently absorb any excess fluid with a cotton swab or gauze.
Cut a piece of SurgiLux film to 7 x 9 mm.
Carefully place the SurgiLux film lengthways across the bisected piece of tissue.
Press down gently on the SurgiLux film with a dry cotton swab.
Activate SurgiLux films using an infra-red diode laser set at 120 mW.
Use appropriate safety glasses for personnel during laser activation.
Start irradiation in the corner of the SurgiLux film.
Pass the beam spot over the green film at a rate of approximately 1 mm per second with a 1 mm diameter beam spot size.
Repeat the irradiation process two more times.
Secure the ends of the tissue in the clamps of a tensile testing instrument.
Separate the tissue pieces at a rate of 1 mm per second until they completely separate.
